input.question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick
input.ground_truth: Because it can. Moving from extreme temperatures one to another can weaken your immune system and that makes it easier for you to get sick. So while it won't directly make you sick to be out in the cold, going between temps is what will do it. Unless it's something like hypothermia. That can make you sick just from being out in the cold.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a cozy blanket. When you are cold, your blanket gets a little thin. Some people think that if you get too cold or swim in very cold water, it makes it easy for germs (tiny bugs that can make you sick) to sneak into your body and make you feel yucky.

But really, it’s not the cold itself that makes you sick—it’s the germs. When you are cold, your body isn’t as good at fighting off those germs. So if you touch something icky or someone sneezes near you, the germs can make you sick more easily. That’s why some people think being cold makes you sick, but actually, it’s the germs that do it!
